CEFR A1.1 · Macro-Unit 01 · Lesson 01

The Story Behind Your Name

Long full names, family nicknames, and tricky spelling: master clear first impressions using I / you, To Be (am / are), and my / your.

Module 01 · Authentic Dilemma

Real Name vs. Nickname: What Is True for You?

Select the card that matches your name story.

USA Pragmatic Chunks [L]:
1) “Call me [Name].” — Natural way to state your preferred name.
2) “Nice to put a face to the name.” — Friendly chunk when meeting someone in person for the first time.

Module 03 · Grammar Mechanics

I / You + To Be (am / are) + My / Your

Exact affirmative, negative, and question forms for introductions.

1 · Self (I / My)
I am / I'm · I am not / I'm not
(+): I am Carlos. / I'm Carlos.
(-): I am not Pollo. / I'm not Pollo.
Possessive: My nickname is Lupe.
2 · Partner (You / Your)
You are / You're · You aren't
(+): You are Sarah. / You're Sarah.
(-): You are not Sara. / You aren't Sara.
Possessive: Your name is easy!
3 · Questions & Short Answers
Are you...? · What's your...?
Q: Are you Carlos?
A (+): Yes, I am. (never Yes, I'm.)
A (-): No, I'm not. I'm Luis.
Q: What's your nickname?
A1.1 Boundary Note: Capitalize I always (I'm, Yes, I am). Use my + noun (my name) and your + noun (your nickname). Zero action verbs in L01!
Module 04 · Audio Investigation

First Contact: Unclear vs. Clear

Compare both introductions and listen to the clear A1.1 standard.

Introduction A · Unclear

Person 1: “Hi. Guadalupe. No, Lupe.”
Person 2: “Sara.”
Person 1: “S-A-R-A?”
Person 2: “No. H.”

Introduction B · Clear A1.1 Standard

Lupe: “Hello! My name is José Guadalupe, but call me Lupe.”
Sarah: “Hi, Lupe! I'm Sarah. S-A-R-A-H. Nice to put a face to the name!”
Lupe: “Are you Sara without H?”
Sarah: “No, I'm not. My first name is S-A-R-A-H.”

Listen to Introduction B (slow, clear A1.1 audio)

First meeting in person after a WhatsApp chat. Which greeting is natural?
Complete the dialogue with am / are / My / your:
Alex: Hello! name is Alejandro, but call me Alex.
Bea: Hi, Alex! you Alex with X?
Alex: Yes, I ! A-L-E-X. And what's name?
Module 06 · Name Card Mission

My Name & Nickname Card (Individual Evidence)

Write 3–4 short sentences in English (real or fictional data). Zero action verbs!

Include: 1) Hello! My name is... / I'm... · 2) My nickname is... / Call me... · 3) Spelling (e.g. L-U-P-E) · 4) I'm not... or Nice to put a face to the name!

Faculty Pedagogical Guide (Documento Rector Secc. 3)

1. Curricular Target

Code: A1.1-U01-L01 (45–60 min) · The Story Behind Your Name.
Foco: Presentarse, deletrear y explicar preferencia de nombre/apodo sin usar verbos de acción.

2. Language Control (P / P? / N / F)

  • P: Hello, Hi, What's your name?, My name is..., Thank you, Again, please, alfabeto A–Z.
  • P?: Deletreo letra por letra; distinción first name / nickname.
  • N: I / you + To Be (am / am not / 'm / 'm not / are / aren't / Are you...?) + my / your; USA Chunks [L]: “Call me [Name]”, “Nice to put a face to the name”.
  • F (Prohibido): Verbos de acción (like, love, hate, live, work, come, have, want, spell con do), tercera persona (L02), Where are you from? (L02).

3. Answer Keys & Rubric (E0–E3)

  • Keys: Item 1: B · Item 2: B · Item 3: A · Item 4: My, Are, am, your.
  • E0: Palabra aislada o error estructural (Yes, I'm / I are).
  • E1: Se presenta pero omite deletreo/apodo o introduce verbos de acción.
  • E2/E3: Precisión en I / you + To Be + my / your, deletreo claro y chunk [L] natural.
